summary: Architect / Adversary / Experimentalist debate + Monte Carlo simulation to push the pricing algorithm error rate toward zero

v1.spec:
DEFINITIONS AND PLANES
Let B = Day1_base for the pivot group (cheapest GM group in the cell), d = rentalDays, r = weekly rule fraction (e.g. -0.7848). FMX plane: R(r) = B x d x (1+r), exact to the cent (verified). Shelf plane: P_served = R(r) x M(t,cell,hour) x k_draw, where k_draw = 0.88 iff the draw carries the 'before' field (campaign), else 1.0. M is fleet-uniform per draw (+-0.01%), so ONE GM price per probe pins the whole fleet; competitors in a draw are exact truth (they never vary). All intent math runs on the SHOPPER (black) price per the settled band contract.

Per-cell state: {r_live, M_ewma, M_last, k_policy, campaign_history[4], C_ladder (competitor prices + timestamps), margin m, tier in {CRITICAL, ACTIVE, TAIL}, b_drift (adaptive buffer), fail_count_24h, state}.
Per-station state: TURBULENT flag = true for TURB_WIN=30 min after ANY FMX write to the station (measured: draw lottery is episodic and write-correlated; 30/30 identical draws in quiet windows).

STATE MACHINE (per cell)
IDLE -> DECIDING -> GRACE -> VERIFYING -> LOCKED -> {DRIFT_WATCH -> CORRECTING -> GRACE ...} | {AT_RISK -> CORRECTING} | STUCK | INFEASIBLE. INFEASIBLE and STUCK require operator ack to leave. All probes drain a global token bucket (refill 2/min, burst 6) with priority P0 verify > P1 correct/decide > P2 critical monitor > P3 active monitor > P4 tail monitor > P5 hour-curve survey; a starved lower class defers, never drops silently.

===== DECIDE (write time) =====
1. Compile the operator intent to an interval [F, T] on the pivot's shopper price. "Just under cheapest": T = 0.97 x C1, F = max(0.95 x C1, C1 - 10 CHF). Rank-K intents compile the same way from the ladder (threshold = comp[10-K] etc.). Fleet-uniformity means solving for the pivot solves the fleet.
2. Measurement bundle: competitor ladder C may come from cache if age <= 30 min (competitors are draw-stable); M may NOT be cached beyond M_STALE=10 min (measured fact: history cannot predict M). Take 2 draws 60-120 s apart at the canonical hour (09:00). From each draw: k_draw from 'before' presence; M_i = P_served / (k_draw x R(r_live)).
3. Agreement test: if |M_1/M_2 - 1| <= TOL_GEN = 0.35%, set M_hat = mean. Else (split -> propagation/generation lottery active): take a third draw after 90 s, use the modal pair; if all three distinct, set M_hat = max(M_i) (conservative for the under-C direction) and mark the decision TURBULENT-sourced.
4. k_policy = 0.88 if any of the last 4 draws on this cell within 24 h carried 'before', else 1.0.
5. Feasibility gate: require (T - F) >= 2 x (0.5 CHF + sigma_cell x T), where sigma_cell = max(0.35%, observed same-window M wobble on this cell). If it fails, enter INFEASIBLE: tell the operator the intent is narrower than the market's noise floor and quote the coin-flip error (approx 50% at the boundary); proceed only on explicit override.
6. Aim point: A = max( T x (1 - b_drift) - 0.5 CHF , (T + F)/2 ). b_drift starts at 0.75% for CRITICAAL-tier monitoring (60-min probes) and 1.5% for ACTIVE (240-min), and is adaptive (see CORRECT step 20).
7. Solve r_new = A / (B x d x M_hat x k_policy) - 1. Round to FMX's 2-decimal percent. If |r_new - r_live| < DEADBAND = 0.6 rule-points, do NOT write (expected shelf move is inside the wobble; a write only buys a propagation lottery). Report "already in band".
8. Write hygiene (hard rules): restate vehicleIds (all groups) AND groupLabel on every update; duration operator via ruleOpFor(duration, openDuration) - never flip an existing '>=' to '='; one write at a time; record {t_write, r_old, r_new, M_hat, k_policy, J_expected = (1+r_new)/(1+r_old)}. Set station TURBULENT until t_write + 30 min. Enter GRACE.

===== VERIFY (the landing) =====
9. T_grace = 15 min after t_write (measured propagation 2-10 min, sometimes longer). Errors inside grace are excluded by definition but verification still runs. Verify probes (1 draw each, P0 priority) at t_write + 4, + 8, + 14 min.
10. Classify each draw (syncClassify): served ratio rho = P_served / (k_draw x B x d). Candidate generations g in {old, new} give implied M_g = rho / (1+r_g). Assign the generation whose implied M is plausible (within [0.985, 1.11]) and closer to M_hat. If |r_new - r_old| < 1.5 rule-points the generations are indistinguishable from M drift: skip classification and use direct position-checking only (step 11) with 2 agreeing draws.
11. Landing is CONFIRMED when 2 consecutive draws classify NEW (or, in indistinguishable mode, agree within TOL_GEN) AND the position predicate passes: F - 0.5 CHF <= P_shop <= T + 0.5 CHF against the freshly seen ladder (the +-0.5 CHF absorbs the site's whole-franc rounding). On confirm: M_ewma := implied M of the landing draws, state := LOCKED, schedule monitoring.
12. Still serving OLD at +14 min: extend once, probes at +19 and +24. Still OLD at +24: state := STUCK, alert operator ("propagation stuck: rentalcars still serving old rule on this hour key"), continue probing every 10 min up to +60; error clock for this cell starts at t_write + 15 (grace end) per the definition.
13. Landed but position FAILS (M moved during propagation): go straight to CORRECT (step 18) with the fresh M - this does not count as a monitor-detected failure but DOES count toward fail_count_24h churn control.

===== MONITOR (the drifting M) =====
14. Tiers and periods: CRITICAL (pickup <= 7 days out, or operator-flagged, or fail_count_24h >= 2): 60 min. ACTIVE (8-30 days): 240 min. TAIL (31+): 1440 min. One draw per probe. Budget proof: e.g. 20 critical + 100 active + 200 tail = 20x24 + 100x6 + 200x1 = 1280 probes/day = 0.9/min average, under the 2/min bucket and well under the 4-6/min ceiling; the bucket enforces it regardless of fleet size by deferring P3/P4.
15. Each probe updates: k flag, competitor ladder (exact), M_draw = P_served/(k_draw x R(r_live)), M_ewma := 0.3 x M_draw + 0.7 x M_ewma, margin m = min(T_now - P_shop_now, P_shop_now - F_now)/T_now with T_now, F_now recomputed from the FRESH ladder (targets move when competitors move - competitor moves are real on one draw).
16. Single-draw trust rule: trust one draw iff station is not TURBULENT AND implied M in [0.985, 1.11] AND no predicate flip. DEMAND a confirmation draw (60-120 s later) before believing: any PASS->FAIL flip, any campaign-flag flip, |M_draw/M_ewma - 1| > 2.0%, or any draw taken while TURBULENT. Never act on a single failing draw - the 2.7% generation / 12% shape lotteries would otherwise write phantom corrections.
17. Triggers out of LOCKED:
    a. AT_RISK (confirmed FAIL): two draws agree the predicate is violated -> CORRECT now.
    b. DRIFT_WATCH (preempt): m < M_MIN = 0.75% AND the last 3 probes show M moving against the margin -> CORRECT before violation. Preempt may only DISCOUNT (rule down); a RAISE (floor defense) always requires a confirmed FAIL, per the never-raise-except-floor doctrine.
    c. Campaign flip: 'before' appearing/disappearing must be stable across 2 probes >= 30 min apart before k_policy flips and a rewrite is considered (the campaign comes and goes per day - do not chase intraday flicker). Meanwhile the cell shows AT_RISK-campaign to the operator. Floor breaches caused ONLY by k=0.88 on a list price that is itself in band are logged as CAMPAIGN_FLOOR warnings, not auto-raised (raising would price the clean segment above T); auto-raise only if the operator enabled strict-floor mode.
    d. Hour-curve survey (P5, CRITICAL cells only, optional per cell): 2 extra draws/day at 11:00 and 15:00 maintain Delta_hour = max_h M_h - M_09. Default prior 3.5% until measured (observed up to 6.85%).
18. All-hours assurance mode (opt-in per cell): the actuator is ONE percent covering all 24 hours, and M varies by hour up to 6.85% - a two-sided band narrower than Delta_hour is physically unreachable. Mode logic: if Delta_hour <= (T-F)/T, aim with M_ref = M_ewma + Delta_hour/2 (centered); else offer only the one-sided contract "under C at all hours": aim A = T x (1 - b_drift) - 0.5 CHF computed with M_ref = M_ewma + Delta_hour (worst hour), floor checked at write time only, shelf dips below F at low-M hours logged not corrected (M is rentalcars' margin; GM's realized revenue R(r) is unchanged, so the dip costs nothing real). Default for all cells remains canonical-hour (09:00) assurance - it is the console's decision unit everywhere.

===== CORRECT =====
19. Re-run DECIDE steps 1-8 with current M_ewma (refreshed: the triggering confirmed draws count as the fresh bundle), current ladder, current k_policy. Anti-churn guards: DEADBAND 0.6 rule-points; minimum spacing REWRITE_MIN = 45 min between writes to the same cell (every write re-opens a 15-min lottery window - chasing a drifting M with writes manufactures error minutes); manual operator writes bypass spacing but not hygiene.
20. Escalation ladder: each confirmed post-landing failure increments fail_count_24h. At 2: promote to CRITICAL monitoring and b_drift += 0.5% (cap 2.5%). At 3 within 24 h: alert operator - this cell's M volatility exceeds the band; quote the achievable contract (e.g. "holds 'under C' but not the 95% floor") and hold at the conservative edge (aim (T+F)/2 with b_drift = 2.5%) until acked. De-escalation: 48 h clean halves b_drift toward its tier default and demotes tier if dates allow.
21. Error accounting (continuous, honest): each cell logs violation-minutes = confirmed-FAIL time minus grace windows, divided by monitored time; the console surfaces realized error rate per tier next to the claimed rate so drift in the market model is visible, not assumed away.

WHY THIS SHAPE: a static guarantee against M_max = 1.0853 holds 6/6 backtested observations but burns up to 7.8% margin permanently; the point policy (today's math) broke rank 5/6. The measure->decide->verify->correct loop with a 0.75-1.5% adaptive buffer is the economic optimum the measurements support: fresh M at decision (it is unpredictable), jump detection via syncClassify (rule changes are jumps, M is continuous), confirmation only where lotteries live (turbulence, flips), and all of it inside 2 probes/min.

knobs.name: T_grace
knobs.value: 15 min after any FMX write (per cell)
knobs.why: Measured propagation is 2-10 min, sometimes longer; 15 min covers the bulk without hiding real landing failures. Matches the error definition's exclusion window.

knobs.name: verify_schedule
knobs.value: 1 draw at +4, +8, +14 min; extension +19, +24; STUCK alert at +24; probe every 10 min to +60
knobs.why: Front-loads confirmation inside grace (most flips land 2-10 min), caps verify cost at 3-5 probes per write, and names stuck propagation instead of silently waiting.

knobs.name: TOL_GEN (same-generation tolerance)
knobs.value: 0.35% on served ratio / implied M
knobs.why: Within a generation draws are identical to +-0.01% fleet-wide plus sub-franc base wobble (~0.3%); generations sit 1.3-2.8% apart. 0.35% separates the two populations cleanly.

knobs.name: generation_indistinguishable_cutoff
knobs.value: |r_new - r_old| < 1.5 rule-points -> skip classification, verify by position with 2 agreeing draws
knobs.why: Below 1.5% a rule jump is the same size as M drift/generation wobble; classification would be noise. Position is what the intent is about anyway.

knobs.name: implied_M_plausibility
knobs.why: Observed M range is [1.0065, 1.0853]; the widened window rejects mis-classified generations and campaign-flag parsing errors without rejecting genuine new extremes.

knobs.name: M_STALE (decision freshness)
knobs.value: M must be <= 10 min old at DECIDE; competitor ladder cache OK to 30 min
knobs.why: Measured: history cannot predict M (7.8% cell-to-cell, 3.56% intra-day drift), so writes need a fresh M; competitors never vary between draws, so their cache is safe at the existing ttlMin=30.

knobs.name: decide_bundle
knobs.value: 2 draws 60-120 s apart; 3rd draw on disagreement; max(M) if all split
knobs.why: Two agreeing draws defeat the episodic generation/shape lottery at minimum cost (quiet windows agree 30/30); max(M) is the conservative choice for the under-C direction during turbulence.

knobs.name: TURB_WIN (station turbulence window)
knobs.value: 30 min after any FMX write to the station; all single draws inside it demand confirmation
knobs.why: The draw lottery is write-correlated and episodic: 30/30 identical draws in quiet windows, 1.3-2.8% split draws around writes. Confirmation only where the lottery actually lives keeps probe cost flat.

knobs.name: b_drift (placement buffer)
knobs.value: 0.75% (CRITICAL, 60-min monitor) / 1.5% (ACTIVE, 240-min); adaptive +0.5% per repeated failure, cap 2.5%; plus fixed 0.5 CHF rounding allowance
knobs.why: Worst measured intra-band drift ~3.56%/day ~= 0.45%/h; buffer must cover drift over (monitor interval + correction latency ~15 min). 0.5 CHF covers the site's whole-franc rounding.

knobs.name: monitor_periods
knobs.value: CRITICAL 60 min / ACTIVE 240 min / TAIL 1440 min; CRITICAL = pickup <= 7 days, operator-flagged, or 2+ fails in 24 h
knobs.why: Bounds violation exposure to <= detection interval + 3 min on the cells that matter commercially while keeping a 320-cell fleet at ~0.9 probes/min.

knobs.name: probe_budget
knobs.value: Global token bucket: refill 2/min, burst 6; priority verify > correct > critical > active > tail > hour-survey
knobs.why: Hard 429 discipline (must stay well under 4-6/min through one relay + single Cloud Run instance); priorities guarantee verification never starves behind routine monitoring.

knobs.name: single_draw_trust
knobs.value: Trust 1 draw iff: not TURBULENT, implied M in [0.985,1.11], no predicate/campaign flip, |M_draw/M_ewma - 1| <= 2.0%. Otherwise demand a 2nd draw 60-120 s later. Never act on a single failing draw.
knobs.why: Quiet windows are deterministic (30/30), so routine probes cost 1 draw; the 2.7% generation and 12% shape lotteries make any single surprising draw untrustworthy - and a phantom FAIL would trigger a real write.

knobs.name: M_ewma_alpha
knobs.why: Tracks the measured 0.45%/h drift within 2-3 probes without letting one lottery draw yank the estimate 2%.

knobs.name: M_MIN (preempt margin)
knobs.value: Correct preemptively when margin < 0.75% of T AND last 3 probes drift against it; preempt may only discount, never raise
knobs.why: Catches continuous drift before it becomes a violation (drift is a ramp, so violations from ramps cost ~0 error minutes); raise-on-guess is forbidden because a wrong raise gives away rank - floor defense waits for a confirmed FAIL.

knobs.name: DEADBAND + REWRITE_MIN
knobs.value: No write if |r_new - r_live| < 0.6 rule-points; >= 45 min between writes to the same cell
knobs.why: Sub-0.6% moves are inside the wobble - a write buys only a fresh 15-min propagation lottery. Spacing stops the loop from chasing a drifting M and manufacturing grace windows.

knobs.name: campaign_handling
knobs.value: Per-draw: divide by that draw's own k (0.88 iff 'before' present) for all M math. Policy k = 0.88 if any campaign draw in last 4 probes/24 h. Rewrite on flip only after the flag is stable across 2 probes >= 30 min apart. Campaign-only floor breaches: WARN, no auto-raise (unless strict-floor mode).
knobs.why: The x0.88 is flagged in-data so M estimation stays exact through it; the campaign comes and goes per day, so persistence-gating stops intraday flip-flop writes; auto-raising against a campaign would misprice the clean segment above T.

knobs.name: feasibility_gate
knobs.value: Refuse (with quoted coin-flip error) any intent where (T - F) < 2 x (0.5 CHF + sigma_cell x T), sigma_cell = max(0.35%, cell wobble)
knobs.why: A 0.5%-wide placement sits INSIDE the generation wobble and franc rounding - the audit already called it a structural coin flip. Saying 'infeasible, here is the achievable contract' beats silently failing half the time.

knobs.name: hour_spread (all-hours mode)
knobs.value: Default assurance = canonical 09:00. Opt-in all-hours: maintain Delta_hour via 2 survey draws/day (11:00, 15:00; prior 3.5%); two-sided band only if Delta_hour <= band width, else one-sided 'under C' aiming at M_ewma + Delta_hour, floor checked at write time only
knobs.why: One rule % covers all 24 hours while M varies up to 6.85% by hour - a 2%-wide band cannot be held at every hour by any policy. Shelf dips below floor at low-M hours cost GM nothing real (M is rentalcars' margin; GM's revenue is the FMX-plane price), so the one-sided contract is the honest sellable one.

knobs.name: escalation
knobs.value: 2 confirmed fails/24 h -> CRITICAL tier + b_drift +0.5%; 3 fails -> operator alert with achievable-contract quote, hold at (T+F)/2 with b_drift 2.5%; 48 h clean -> decay toward defaults
knobs.why: Cells whose local M volatility exceeds the band must widen their buffer or renegotiate the intent - more writes cannot fix variance, they add grace windows.

v1.claimed_error: Canonical-hour contract (09:00 decision plane, the console's existing decision unit), CRITICAL tier (60-min monitoring): expected violation rate ~1-2.5% of shopper moments per cell. Derivation: ramp drift (~0.45%/h measured) is caught by the preempt trigger before violation (~0 error minutes); step events beyond the 0.75-1.5% buffer occur <= ~1-2/day (measured regime shifts up to 3.56%), only the adverse-direction half count, and each costs at most detection (<= 60 min) + confirm (~2 min) + write (~1 min) minus the 15-min grace exclusion => <= ~48 violation-min per event, ~24-96 min/day worst case = 1.7-6.7%, halved in practice because roughly half of steps are absorbed by the buffer or preempted => 1-2.5%. ACTIVE tier (240-min monitoring) scales detection linearly: ~3-6%. All-hours contract: the one-sided 'under C at every hour' variant holds ~97-98% of shopper moments at a mean extra-discount cost of about Delta_hour/2 (1.5-3.5%); a two-sided 2%-wide band across all hours is INFEASIBLE on cells with hour spread like the measured 6.85% and is refused, not attempted. Assumptions: M dynamics as measured on 2026-08-29/30 (quiet-window determinism; drift <= ~0.5%/h typical; steps <= ~3.6%, <= 2/day; M in [0.99, 1.09]); propagation <= 15 min for >= 90% of writes (excess surfaces as STUCK alerts, and error-clock time past grace is counted, not hidden); campaign always flagged via 'before'; competitors draw-stable; probe budget 2/min honored; intent band at least 2 x (0.5 CHF + wobble) wide - narrower intents are refused with a quoted ~50% coin-flip error rather than silently failed. Irreducible floor under all assumptions: whole-franc rounding + 0.35% generation wobble means no policy can place more precisely than ~+-0.5 CHF +-0.35%; the claimed rates are against intents that respect that floor, and the console reports realized violation-minutes per tier so the claim is continuously audited against reality.

questions.q: Your DEADBAND, generation-indistinguishable cutoff, and escalation are all denominated in absolute rule-points, but shelf impact scales as Δr/(1+r). At your own example rule r=-0.7848, 0.6 rule-points = 0.006/0.2152 = 2.79% of shelf price — wider than the entire 2% band [0.95·C1, 0.97·C1]. What happens when a CONFIRMED-FAIL cell needs a 1.5% shelf correction that is only 0.32 rule-points, i.e. inside DEADBAND? Step 19 re-runs step 7, which reports 'already in band' while the predicate is confirmed violated. Which wins, and what state does the cell enter?
questions.why: This is a dimensional bug, not a tuning choice: at deep discounts every needed correction is refused and every permitted write overshoots the band. Conversely at shallow rules (1+r≈0.95) the 1.5-point cutoff = 1.58% shelf, inside the 1.3-2.8% generation lottery, so classification is skipped exactly where it works and trusted exactly where it fails. All jump knobs must be respecified in J-space (J=(1+r_new)/(1+r_old), which you already compute as J_expected) and DEADBAND must be waived on confirmed FAIL.

questions.q: Which plane does the contract legally bind on: the 2-decimal API price, or the whole-franc price and list position the shopper actually sees? What is rentalcars' rounding function (half-up? truncation? you never measured it) and its tie-break rule when GM and C1 display the same franc? Your ±0.5 CHF allowance silently assumes half-up rounding and assumes ties are wins.
questions.why: ERROR is defined at the shopper's eyes. If RC truncates, GM at 51.42 and C1 at 51.99 both display 51 — a tie with unknown ordering — while your predicate passes cleanly. On sub-80-CHF cells the 1-franc display quantum exceeds your entire 0.35% wobble budget, so the display plane, not M, is the binding noise source there. One cheap experiment (scan API decimals vs displayed francs across a day of cached draws) settles the rounding function; the spec ships without it.

questions.q: Compile the intent for C1 = 400 CHF (a real ZRH case: the 13-day 400-CHF field in autoscan-margin-floor.md): F = max(380, 390) = 390 > T = 388. The interval is INVERTED, not narrow — your INFEASIBLE message ('intent narrower than noise floor, ~50% coin-flip') is a misdiagnosis, and production semantics (pricing-band-2026-08-28.md: factor clamped UP to max(floors), floor wins) resolve it differently. Combined with the feasibility gate killing C1 < 75.7 (width 0.02·C1 < 2×(0.5+0.0035·T)) and C1 > 244.6 (width 10−0.03·C1), your defined domain is C1 ∈ [~76, ~245]. Was that intended, and what does the algorithm aim at when the operator overrides — the spec defines no contract at all for overridden cells?
questions.why: Short economy cells (memory: 1-3 day cells against 40-80 CHF fields) and long/premium cells (400+ CHF) are both real, documented ZRH segments — and both sit outside the algorithm's domain from day one. The claimed 1-2.5% error rate covers only the mid-priced minority; the majority of fleet-days run in an undefined override mode the error ledger says nothing about.

questions.q: Your claimed 1-2.5% is explicitly 'canonical-hour (09:00) contract' — but the ERROR definition is a random SHOPPER moment, and shoppers choose their own pickup hour (the console itself rotates 19 pickup rungs, RC_TIMES). M is hour-dependent by up to +6.85% while competitors are hour-identical. What is your claimed error rate under the stated definition, integrated over the pickup-hour distribution? And is the operator ever told that the default 'just under C' contract holds only for 09:00-pickup shoppers?
questions.why: Aim A ≈ 0.9625·C1 at M_09=1.0065 lands at 0.9625×1.0685 = 1.028·C1 for a 15:00-pickup query — ABOVE the cheapest competitor all day for that hour band, invisible to a monitor that only samples 09:00, and never logged by the step-21 ledger. Making all-hours mode opt-in is a metric redefinition, not an error rate. For rank intents the one-sided worst-hour aim (M_ewma + Δ_hour) must be the DEFAULT, and Δ_hour needs more than 3 sampled hours of 19 with a 3.5% prior against a measured 6.85%.

questions.q: Who owns k_policy? Step 4 says 0.88 if ANY of the last 4 draws in 24h carried 'before'; 17c says the flag may only flip after being stable across 2 probes ≥30 min apart. These give different answers for at least 30-60 minutes after every campaign transition — and the campaign 'comes and goes per day', so this is a daily event, not an edge case. Walk the exact state sequence for a campaign-OFF morning (scenario attached) and bound the violation minutes.
questions.why: The two rules compound with the DEADBAND bug: after the mispriced write lands +13.6% high, CORRECT re-runs step 4, k_policy is still 0.88 (yesterday's draws are within 24h), so r_new ≈ r_live → DEADBAND → 'already in band' reported on a cell serving 9% above the cheapest competitor. The fix is one owner: k_policy must follow per-draw evidence at DECIDE/VERIFY time (the verify draws ARE 2 agreeing fresh observations, not intraday flicker), with the 30-min stability gate reserved for unsolicited monitor flips.

questions.q: Where is the FMX-plane change detector? R(r_live) has at least four inputs that change without your loop writing anything: manual weekly-rule edits in the DPS UI, Excel base-ladder syncs (rate1..31, the documented live workflow in fmx-price-override-write.md), the ×0.55 promotion factor in the verified price chain (which your R(r)=B·d·(1+r) formula omits entirely unless B is silently defined as post-promotion), and 18 of 30 base overrides expiring 1/1/2027. Every one of these silently corrupts every implied-M computation. FMX reads cost zero relay probes — why does the spec never schedule them?
questions.why: A hand edit of -5 rule-points at (1+r)=0.53 makes implied M = 0.949 — outside [0.985,1.11], so BOTH generation candidates are implausible and step 10 has no defined outcome (false STUCK at best). A smaller edit lands inside the window, poisons M_ewma by 2-3%, and triggers phantom corrections that write-war with the operator, each write buying a fresh 15-min lottery. Full FMX read access is the one free sensor you have; a 5-min rules/bases poll plus 'external write detected → re-baseline r_live, mark TURBULENT' closes the whole class.

questions.q: What is burst mode? Competitor repricing is CORRELATED across cells (one December reprice moves C1 on a hundred cells overnight — and your claimed-error derivation budgets zero events for competitor moves at all, only M steps). With 2-draw confirmation per cell, per-cell verify, and a 2/min bucket, ~120 flipped cells need ~600 P0/P1 draws = 5 hours of saturation while all monitoring starves and every write's TURBULENT window doubles the cost of the trickle that remains. What is the realized error rate on that day, and where does the spec exploit the fact that one probe returns the FULL competitor ladder for its cell — or that adjacent-duration cells share most of their competitor field?
questions.why: The 0.9 probes/min budget proof assumes independent per-cell events; the binding constraint is the correlated day, which is also the commercially critical day. Without station-level triage (rank cells by revenue-at-risk, batch-write, verify a sample rather than every cell), realized error on a market-move day is ~15-25% on ACTIVE cells vs the claimed 3-6% — and the step-21 ledger will publish that contradiction in week one.

questions.q: Where is the DEGRADED state? The relay is one home machine, and your own ops history (cloudrun-429-single-instance.md) shows both relay workers dropping silently for 20-40 min after 429 storms — triggered by exactly the mass-write days when you most need probes. During an outage: verify probes at +4/+8/+14 are missed (STUCK false alarm or silent extension?), M_STALE=10min invalidates every queued DECIDE on arrival, DRIFT_WATCH's 'last 3 probes' spans pre-outage data, and 'defer, never drop' becomes 'defer forever' with no alarm. Also: ACTIVE-tier b_drift=1.5% is arithmetically insufficient by your own knob formula — 0.45%/h × (240min interval + 15min latency) = 1.93%.
questions.why: The claimed error assumes 100% measurement uptime; the measured system does not have it. A blind-time rule is cheap to specify: widen the effective buffer by 0.45%/h × (time since last trusted draw), freeze non-P0 writes past 20 min blind, alert past 30, and log blind-time separately in the ledger instead of counting it as monitored-clean. And either raise ACTIVE b_drift to ≥2% or shorten the tier to 180 min — currently ramps alone beat the buffer on ACTIVE cells with no step event needed.

scenarios.name: Deadband deadlock at deep discount (confirmed violation, no legal write)
scenarios.setup: Cell: C1=150, T=145.50, F=142.50, band width 3 CHF (2%). Deep-rule group: r_live=-0.7848, (1+r)=0.2152 (the spec's own example). DECIDE aims A=(T+F)/2=144.00 at M_hat=1.048; landing confirmed, LOCKED. Overnight M drifts +1.7% (measured intra-day drift reaches +3.56%): served = 144.00×1.017 = 146.45 > T+0.5 = 146.00. Two monitor draws agree → AT_RISK → CORRECT.

attack1.verdict: The skeleton is right and should survive: measure-fresh-M-then-solve, jump-vs-drift separation via syncClassify, confirmation only where the lotteries live, a priority token bucket, and an honest realized-error ledger are all correct responses to the measured physics. But the spec as written cannot deliver its claimed 1-2.5%, for six reasons, four of which are structural rather than tuning. (1) DIMENSIONAL BUG: DEADBAND and the generation cutoff live in rule-point space while every effect lives in J=(1+r_new)/(1+r_old) space; at the spec's own r=-0.7848, the 0.6-point deadband is 2.79% of shelf — wider than the entire 2% band — so confirmed violations at deep discounts have NO legal correction and the state machine has no exit (Scenario 1, compounded in Scenario 2). Respecify all jump knobs in J-space and waive DEADBAND on confirmed FAIL. (2) METRIC REDEFINITION: the error definition is a random shopper moment, shoppers choose pickup hours, M varies +6.85% by hour while competitors don't; the default 09:00-only contract lets a cell run ~40-60% true error while the ledger reports ~1-2% (Scenario 3). For rank intents the worst-hour one-sided aim must be the default, and the ledger must sample off-canonical hours or the claim is unauditable. (3) DOMAIN HOLE: the band compile is INFEASIBLE below C1≈76, above C1≈245, and outright inverted (F>T) above 333 — excluding the two segments memory shows are the real business (short economy, long premium), with no defined behavior for overridden cells (Scenario 6). Fix the compile (quantized display plane, measured RC rounding + tie rule, floor-wins clamp semantics matching production) before quoting any error rate. (4) TWO CONTRADICTORY OWNERS of k_policy make every campaign-OFF morning a 30-60-min, +13.6% rank-loss event (Scenario 2); one owner, per-draw evidence at write/verify time. (5) NO EXTERNAL-CHANGE DETECTOR for the FMX plane despite free, zero-relay-cost read access — manual edits, Excel base syncs, the ×0.55 promotion (absent from the spec's R(r) formula), and expiring overrides all silently corrupt M math into false-STUCK or operator write-wars (Scenario 4); a 5-min FMX poll plus re-baseline closes the class. (6) INDEPENDENCE AND UPTIME ASSUMPTIONS contradicted by the project's own ops history: correlated market moves saturate the bucket for ~5 h at ~15-25% realized error, and the single-relay outages that accompany exactly those days have no DEGRADED state, so blind time is counted as clean (Scenario 5); add burst triage (revenue-ranked, batch writes, sampled verification, shared-ladder reuse across adjacent durations) and a blind-time rule (buffer widens 0.45%/h of blindness, writes freeze past 20 min, blind minutes ledgered separately). Secondary fixes: re-baseline M_ewma from a post-TURB_WIN draw rather than landing draws taken inside the lottery; ACTIVE b_drift is arithmetically short of its own drift formula (needs ≥2% or a 180-min tier); the preempt-discount-only doctrine contradicts production's sanctioned in-band upward correction and buys floor-side violation minutes for nothing; max(M) 'conservatism' in a 3-way split is anti-conservative toward the floor side of a two-sided intent. With all of the above amended, the claimed 1-2.5% on feasible contracts is plausible and near-zero (~0.5-1%) is reachable at CRITICAL tier within the same probe budget; without amendments the step-21 ledger itself will falsify the claim within days — on the first campaign-off morning, the first market-move day, or the first hand edit Berkay makes in DPS. v2.spec:
PART A — ANSWERS TO THE ADVERSARY (one per question)

A1 (DEADBAND dimensional bug): Conceded — structural, not tuning. All jump knobs move to J-space, J = (1+r_new)/(1+r_live), shelf effect = |J−1| (already recorded as J_expected). DEADBAND_J = max(0.35%, q/(2P)) with q = 1 CHF display quantum, and it applies ONLY to unsolicited re-aims (drift preempts, routine re-decides). On a CONFIRMED FAIL both DEADBAND and the 45-min spacing are VOID: the transition is AT_RISK → CORRECTING → write the exact solve, which is always expressible because FMX's 2-decimal percent quantizes at 0.01 rule-point = 0.046% shelf even at (1+r)=0.2152. "Already in band" may only be reported when the fresh display-plane predicate PASSES; it can never answer a confirmed violation, so the Scenario-1 deadlock has no path. The generation-indistinguishable cutoff also moves to J-space: syncClassify runs iff |J−1| ≥ 1.0% (generations sit 1.3–2.8% apart in J at every rule depth); below that, position-only verification with 2 agreeing draws. Confirmed FAIL wins, always, and the state entered is CORRECTING.

A2 (binding plane / rounding): The contract binds on what the shopper sees: whole-franc display and list order. Conceded that ρ (rounding) and the tie rule were unmeasured; v2 ships a Day-0, ZERO-probe calibration (S3): replay the console's stored scan history (2-decimal API prices) against displayed francs across a day, fit ρ ∈ {trunc, half-up, ceil} and the tie ordering; recheck monthly. Until calibrated, targets are conservative under both trunc and half-up — P_api ≤ min(⌊C1⌋ − 0.01, round(C1) − 0.51) — and ties count as violations. The flat ±0.5 CHF allowance is deleted; all compile/feasibility math runs on the display grid (D1–D2). Below ~150 CHF the 1-franc quantum is indeed the dominant noise — and it HELPS feasibility there: a ~1-franc-wide preimage dwarfs the 0.18 CHF wobble of a 52 CHF cell.

A3 (domain hole / inverted band): Conceded; fixed in three parts. (i) Inverted band (F > T, C1 ≳ 333, the real 400 CHF case): the compile follows PRODUCTION semantics — floor wins (factor clamps UP to max(floors), per pricing-band-2026-08-28). The contract collapses to the point contract "hold at F = C1 − 10, displayed strictly under C1": aim A = F, predicate [F − q/2, disp(C1) − 1 franc]. Operator message: "floor binds", never "coin flip". (ii) Cheap cells: the quantized compile makes C1 = 52.49 feasible — allowed francs {50, 51}, preimage width ≈ 1.6 CHF ≥ required 2×(σ·P + ρ_resid) ≈ 0.6 CHF. The percent-width gate is replaced by francs-in-band, so the C1 ∈ [~76, ~245] hole disappears; the volume business is inside the domain. (iii) Overridden refusals now run a DEFINED contract: NEAREST_ACHIEVABLE aim (closest achievable point to the requested band), normal buffers and tier, and a dual ledger entry (error vs stated intent AND vs achievable contract). No undefined mode remains.

A4 (hour dependence): Conceded — the 09:00-only default was a metric redefinition. v2 DEFAULT for under-C/rank intents is the ONE-SIDED all-hours contract aiming at M_band_max (max across per-hour-band EWMAs; unmeasured bands assume measured-max + prior Δ_hour = 7% > the measured 6.85%). Hour coverage costs ZERO extra probes: every monitor probe rotates its query hour across 3 bands aligned to the RC_TIMES rungs, and M_ewma is kept per band, so Δ_hour is continuously measured from the existing probe stream instead of a 2-draw/day opt-in survey. The claimed error is quoted hour-integrated over the rung distribution. A two-sided band across all hours is refused whenever Δ_hour > band width. The canonical-hour contract survives only as explicit opt-in, labeled HOUR-CONDITIONAL in the UI and the ledger — the operator is told, in those words, that only canonical-band shoppers are covered.

A5 (k_policy ownership): One owner: k is per-draw evidence, never a policy state. Every M computation divides by its own draw's flag. A write solve uses k_write = the flag agreed by the FRESH decision/verify bundle — two draws minutes apart ARE the stability evidence, not intraday flicker; if they disagree, a 3rd draw decides; still mixed → use the latest draw's flag, mark CAMPAIGN-EDGE, re-probe at 30 min. The "any flagged draw in last 4/24h" rule is DELETED. The 30-min two-probe stability gate survives ONLY for unsolicited monitor-triggered rewrites. Scenario replay: campaign-OFF morning, both 09:00 bundle draws lack 'before' → k_write = 1.0 → the solve is correct, the +13.6% overshoot cannot occur; violation minutes from this class ≈ 0. Residual: a flip between write and next probe is an ordinary step event — flagged in-data, detected at the next probe, corrected with gates void (A1), bounded by the tier detection interval, not hours.

A6 (FMX-plane detector): Conceded — the free sensor is now scheduled (S1). Every 5 min: hash the weekly rules of governed stations (%, groups, name, date spans). Daily (and on-demand whenever implied M is implausible): diff base ladders rate1..31, CHANNEL percentages, and override expiry dates, with a 30-day advance alert for the 18-of-30 1/1/2027 expiries. R(r) is corrected to R = Day1 × d × chan × (1+r) with chan (the ×0.55 promotion channel factor from the verified chain) POLLED, never assumed. On external diff: re-baseline r_live/B_eff, mark station TURBULENT, extend syncClassify's candidate set to ALL generations seen in the horizon {old, A, B, …}, and enter EXTERNAL_EDIT: the loop pauses corrections on that cell and NEVER writes over a human edit — the external value is adopted as the new baseline (or the operator acks a re-take). Write-wars are structurally impossible. Step-10 fallback fixed: all candidates implausible → immediate FMX re-read FIRST; only if FMX is unchanged and a 2nd draw is still implausible → DATA_ANOMALY alert. No false STUCK, no silent draw-discarding.

A7 (burst mode): Added as a station overlay (M7). Enter on ≥8 predicate flips within 30 min, or the SAME competitor moving on ≥5 cells (one probe returns the full exact ladder; adjacent-duration cells share most of the field, so one observed move marks neighbors SUSPECT and reprioritizes them). Inside BURST: (a) 2-draw confirmation is WAIVED for violations > 3σ_cell — a 5–8% C1 drop is not a lottery artifact because competitors never vary; confirmation exists for lottery-sized surprises only; (b) M_ewma reuse allowed to 60 min with the buffer widened 0.45%/h × age — spend ~1% extra discount instead of probes; (c) corrections ranked by revenue-at-risk (pickup proximity × price × cell volume); (d) SAMPLED verification: top decile gets the full +4/+8/+14 schedule, the rest ONE verify draw spread over the following hours, and a failing sample escalates its whole batch to full verify; (e) TURBULENT confirmation-doubling applies only to SURPRISING draws, not expected post-write positions. Worked budget for the 120-cell Monday: ~120 solve draws + ~36 + ~108 verify draws ≈ 264 ≈ 2.2 h at 2/min (vs 5 h unmitigated), top-revenue cells corrected inside ~30 min. Honest burst-day claim: ~5–8% violation-minutes on affected cells that day (vs 15–25% unmitigated), ledgered as a NAMED episode, never blended into the steady-state number.

A8 (DEGRADED state): Added (M6), fed by the existing relay heartbeat (/api/watch-status relayOnline/agoSec). t_blind = time since last trusted draw, per station. Rules: b_eff = b_tier + 0.45%/h × t_blind for any decision on cached data; t_blind > 20 min → freeze non-P0 writes and EXTEND verify timers — a missing probe is "no data", never "old rule": STUCK requires an actually-OLD-classified draw, so outages cannot fake STUCK; t_blind > 30 min → DEGRADED alert + relay kick runbook (launchctl kickstart, per ops memory); DRIFT_WATCH's "last 3 probes" must all be post-gap; blind minutes are ledgered UNMONITORED — never counted as clean — and the published rate carries an uncertainty band over them; recovery runs a P1 re-baseline sweep, CRITICAL cells first. The ACTIVE arithmetic bug is fixed by splitting the tier: one-sided cells 240 min with b = 2.0% (covers 0.45%/h × 4.25 h = 1.91%); strict-floor cells 180 min with b = 1.5% (covers 1.46%). Also folded in from the verdict: M_ewma re-baselines from the first post-TURB_WIN draw (α = 1 on that draw, then 0.3); 3-way-split conservatism is contract-directional (max M for one-sided-under, median + provisional for strict-floor); the preempt may correct in EITHER direction strictly INSIDE the band — matching production's one sanctioned upward correction (pulling a price back above the floor) — while crossing the band top still requires a confirmed FAIL.

PART B — REVISED SPEC v2

PLANES
P1. FMX plane: R(r) = Day1_base × d × chan × (1+r), exact to the cent. chan = the rentalcars channel factor (currently ×0.55 promotion), READ from FMX (S1), never assumed.
P2. API plane: P_api = R(r) × M(cell, hourband, t) × k_draw; k_draw = 0.88 iff THAT draw carries 'before'. M is fleet-uniform per draw (±0.01%) → one GM price per probe pins the fleet; competitor prices in a draw are exact truth.
P3. Display plane (BINDING): P_disp = ρ(P_api) in whole francs; ρ and the equal-franc tie order come from the S3 calibration. ERROR = at a random shopper moment (hour-integrated over the RC_TIMES rung distribution) the displayed position violates the intent, outside the 15-min grace.

STATE
Per cell: {r_live, Day1/chan fingerprint, M_ewma[3 hour bands], Δ_hour, ladder cache (ttl 30 min), contract ∈ {ONE_SIDED (default), STRICT_FLOOR, HOUR_CONDITIONAL (opt-in), NEAREST_ACHIEVABLE (override)}, tier, b_drift, fail_count_24h, state}. Station overlays: TURBULENT (30 min after ANY write — loop or external), BURST, DEGRADED. Global token bucket: refill 2/min, burst 6; priority P0 verify > P1 correct/decide > P2 critical monitor > P3 active > P4 tail; starved classes defer with visible queue age, never drop silently.
State machine: IDLE → DECIDING → GRACE → VERIFYING → LOCKED → {DRIFT_WATCH | AT_RISK} → CORRECTING → GRACE …; exceptional: STUCK, INFEASIBLE, DATA_ANOMALY, EXTERNAL_EDIT (exit by operator ack or baseline adoption).

SENSORS (all zero relay cost)
S1. FMX poll: every 5 min, hash weekly rules of governed stations (%, groups, name, spans). Daily + on-demand (any implausible implied M): diff base ladders rate1..31, channel percentages, override expiries (alert ≥30 days before expiry). External diff → re-baseline r_live/B_eff, station TURBULENT, syncClassify candidates = ALL horizon generations, cell → EXTERNAL_EDIT (corrections paused; human edits adopted, never overwritten without ack).
S2. Relay heartbeat (/api/watch-status) → t_blind per station → M6.
S3. Display calibration, Day 0: fit ρ ∈ {trunc, half-up, ceil} + tie rule from stored API-decimal vs displayed-franc pairs; monthly recheck. Pre-calibration: target P_api ≤ min(⌊C1⌋ − 0.01, round(C1) − 0.51); ties count as violations.

DECIDE
D1. Compile the intent on the display grid. "Just under cheapest": allowed franc set S = {n ∈ ℤ : F ≤ n ≤ disp(C1) − 1}, F = max(0.95×C1, C1 − 10). If F exceeds the top (inverted, C1 ≳ 333): floor-wins point contract (production clamp semantics) — aim A = F, predicate [F − q/2, disp(C1) − 1]. Rank-K intents compile identically against comp[10−K].
D2. Feasibility: W = width(ρ⁻¹(S)); require W ≥ 2 × (σ_cell × P + ρ_resid), σ_cell = max(0.35%, observed cell wobble). Fail → INFEASIBLE, message names the ACHIEVABLE contract; operator override → NEAREST_ACHIEVABLE with dual-ledger accounting.
D3. Freshness: ladder cache ≤ 30 min OK (competitors draw-stable); M ≤ 10 min (≤ 60 min in BURST with widened buffer). Bundle: 2 draws 60–120 s apart at the aim hour band, k per draw from its own flag. |M1/M2 − 1| ≤ TOL_GEN = 0.35% → M_hat = mean; else 3rd draw, modal pair; 3-way split → max(M) for ONE_SIDED, median + provisional for STRICT_FLOOR.
D4. M_ref by contract: ONE_SIDED → max over band EWMAs, unmeasured bands = measured max + Δ_prior 7%; STRICT_FLOOR → mean + Δ_hour/2, offered only if Δ_hour ≤ band width; HOUR_CONDITIONAL → canonical-band EWMA.
D5. Aim: A = max(F_pre, T_pre × (1 − b_eff)); T_pre = upper edge of ρ⁻¹(max S), F_pre = lower edge of ρ⁻¹(min S); b_eff = b_tier + DEGRADED/BURST widening.
D6. Solve r_new = A / (Day1 × d × chan × M_ref × k_write) − 1, round to FMX 2-decimal percent; J = (1+r_new)/(1+r_live).
D7. Gates — unsolicited re-aims ONLY, VOID on confirmed FAIL: skip the write if |J−1| < max(0.35%, q/(2P)) or the expected displayed franc is unchanged; REWRITE_MIN = 45 min per cell.
D8. Hygiene (hard): restate ALL vehicle groups + groupLabel; duration operator via ruleOpFor (never flip '>=' to '='); one write at a time; log {t, r_old→r_new, M_ref, k_write, J}; station TURBULENT 30 min; → GRACE.

VERIFY
V1. T_grace = 15 min. P0 draws at +4, +8, +14. If |J−1| ≥ 1.0%: syncClassify with candidate set = all FMX generations seen in the horizon, per-draw k. Else: position-only, 2 agreeing draws.
V2. All candidates implausible (implied M ∉ [0.985, 1.11]) → immediate S1 re-read BEFORE any transition; FMX unchanged + a 2nd implausible draw → DATA_ANOMALY.
V3. CONFIRMED = 2 draws classify NEW (or agree in position mode) AND the display predicate passes on the fresh ladder → LOCKED. M_provisional from landing draws; the first post-TURB_WIN draw REPLACES it (α = 1), thereafter α = 0.3.
V4. OLD at +14 → extend +19/+24 → STUCK only on actually-OLD-classified draws (missing draws EXTEND timers — DEGRADED semantics); alert; 10-min probes to +60; the error clock runs from grace end.
V5. Landed but predicate FAILS → CORRECTING with the fresh M; D7 gates void; counts toward fail_count_24h churn control, not monitor-detected failures.

MONITOR
M1. Tiers: CRITICAL (pickup ≤ 7 d, flagged, or 2+ fails/24 h) 60 min, b = 0.75%; ACTIVE (8–30 d): one-sided 240 min b = 2.0%, strict-floor 180 min b = 1.5%; TAIL (31+ d) 1440 min. Probe hours ROTATE across 3 bands (morning/midday/evening, aligned to RC_TIMES); per-band EWMA; Δ_hour = spread of band EWMAs, prior 7% until ≥ 5 draws/band. Budget: 20×24 + 100×6 + 200×1 = 1280/day ≈ 0.9/min.
M2. Per probe: per-draw k; exact ladder refresh; M_draw = P_api/(k_draw × R(r_live)); band EWMA update; display predicate + margin recomputed on the FRESH ladder (competitor moves are real on one draw).
M3. Trust: one draw suffices iff not TURBULENT, implied M ∈ [0.985, 1.11], no predicate/campaign flip, |M_draw/M_ewma − 1| ≤ 2%. Otherwise demand a confirming draw 60–120 s later — EXCEPT a violation > 3σ_cell (competitor-move class; ladders never vary) acts on ONE draw. Never write from a single lottery-sized surprise.
M4. AT_RISK: confirmed FAIL (2 draws) or a >3σ single-draw violation → CORRECTING; all gates void.
M5. DRIFT_WATCH: margin < 0.75% of T AND 3 consecutive post-gap probes trending adverse → preemptive in-band correction in EITHER direction (production's sanctioned upward correction back into band); crossing the band TOP always requires a confirmed FAIL.
M6. DEGRADED: b_eff += 0.45%/h × t_blind on cached-data decisions; t_blind > 20 min → freeze non-P0 writes, extend verify timers; > 30 min → alert + relay kick runbook; blind minutes ledgered UNMONITORED; recovery = P1 re-baseline sweep, CRITICAL first.
M7. BURST: enter on ≥8 flips/30 min or same competitor moved on ≥5 cells; SUSPECT propagation to adjacent durations from shared ladders; rank by revenue-at-risk; M reuse ≤ 60 min with widening; sampled verify (top decile full schedule, rest 1 draw each, sample failure escalates its batch); TURBULENT confirmation applies only to surprising draws; exit when the queue drains + one clean sweep; the episode is ledgered by name.
M8. Campaign: k is per-draw everywhere; an unsolicited rewrite on a flip waits for the flag stable across 2 probes ≥ 30 min apart; floor breaches caused only by k = 0.88 on an in-band list price → CAMPAIGN_FLOOR warning, auto-raise only in strict-floor mode.

CORRECT
C1. Re-run D1–D8 with the trigger draws as the fresh bundle (fresh ladder, fresh per-draw k). D7 gates void on confirmed FAIL — a confirmed violation ALWAYS produces a write or an explicit INFEASIBLE/EXTERNAL_EDIT/DEGRADED-freeze alert, never silence.
C2. Escalation: 2 confirmed fails/24 h → CRITICAL + b_drift += 0.5% (cap 2.5%); 3 → operator alert quoting the achievable contract, hold at the conservative edge; 48 h clean → decay toward tier defaults. BURST-episode failures count ONCE per station (a market move must not mass-escalate every cell).
C3. Ledger: violation-minutes / monitored-minutes per tier AND per contract class, hour-integrated (the band rotation makes the sample unbiased); UNMONITORED bucket for blind time; named BURST episodes; dual accounting on NEAREST_ACHIEVABLE cells; realized vs claimed published side by side so the market model is audited, not assumed.

knobs.name: DEADBAND_J (J-space, waivable)
knobs.value: Skip unsolicited write if |J-1| < max(0.35%, q/(2P)), J=(1+r_new)/(1+r_live), q=1 CHF; VOID on confirmed FAIL, where the exact solve is always written
knobs.why: Fixes the dimensional bug: 0.6 rule-points was 2.79% of shelf at r=-0.7848 (wider than the whole band), refusing every needed deep-rule correction. FMX's 0.01-point quantum = 0.046% shelf even there, so a legal write always exists; confirmed violations can never be answered with 'already in band'.

knobs.name: generation_classification_cutoff
knobs.value: syncClassify runs iff |J_expected - 1| >= 1.0%; below, verify by position with 2 agreeing draws
knobs.why: Generations sit 1.3-2.8% apart in J-space at every rule depth; the old 1.5-rule-point cutoff skipped classification where it worked (deep rules) and trusted it where it failed (shallow).

knobs.name: display_calibration (S3)
knobs.value: Day-0 zero-probe fit of rounding rho {trunc, half-up, ceil} + equal-franc tie order from stored API-decimal vs displayed-franc pairs; monthly recheck. Pre-calibration: target P <= min(floor(C1)-0.01, round(C1)-0.51); ties count as violations
knobs.why: The contract binds at the shopper's eyes; the +-0.5 CHF allowance silently assumed half-up and tie-wins. One replay of cached draws settles it; until then targets are safe under both plausible roundings.

knobs.name: quantized_feasibility_gate
knobs.value: Feasible iff width(rho-inverse of allowed franc set) >= 2 x (sigma_cell x P + rho_resid), sigma_cell = max(0.35%, cell wobble); inverted band (F > top, C1 >~ 333) = floor-wins point contract at F (production clamp); genuine refusal + override = NEAREST_ACHIEVABLE with dual ledger
knobs.why: Closes the domain hole: C1=52.49 becomes feasible (francs {50,51}, preimage 1.6 CHF >> 0.6 needed), C1=400 resolves per production semantics (floor wins, 'floor binds' message), and overridden cells get a defined aim, buffer, and ledger instead of an undefined mode.

knobs.name: contract_default + hour bands
knobs.value: Default for under-C/rank intents = ONE_SIDED all-hours, M_ref = max over 3 hour-band EWMAs (prior delta_hour 7% until >=5 draws/band); monitor probes ROTATE query hour across bands (zero extra probes); canonical-hour = opt-in, labeled HOUR-CONDITIONAL in UI and ledger; two-sided all-hours refused when delta_hour > band width
knobs.why: ERROR is a random shopper moment and shoppers pick hours; M varies +6.85% by hour while competitors don't. Worst-band aiming converts hour spread from hidden error (~40-60% on a bad cell) into a visible, bounded margin cost; rotation measures delta_hour from the existing probe stream for free.

knobs.name: k ownership (campaign x0.88)
knobs.value: k is per-draw evidence everywhere; k_write = the flag agreed by the fresh 2-draw bundle (3rd draw on disagreement; still mixed = latest flag + CAMPAIGN-EDGE recheck at 30 min). Last-4-draws/24h rule DELETED; 30-min stability gate applies only to unsolicited monitor-triggered rewrites
knobs.why: One owner. The old dual rule made every campaign-OFF morning a +13.6% overshoot that both rules then blocked from fixing for 35+ minutes. Fresh bundle draws minutes apart ARE stability evidence; the gate remains only where flicker-chasing writes were the risk.

knobs.name: FMX_poll (S1, zero relay cost)
knobs.value: 5-min weekly-rule hash per governed station; daily + on-implausible-M diff of base ladders rate1..31, channel percentages (the x0.55 chan factor is polled, never assumed), and override expiries (alert >=30 days ahead; 18/30 expire 1/1/2027). External diff -> re-baseline + TURBULENT + EXTERNAL_EDIT (never overwrite a human edit); syncClassify candidates = all horizon generations
knobs.why: FMX reads are the one free sensor. Closes the whole ghost-write class: no false STUCK from 3-generation lotteries, no M_ewma poisoning from hand edits, no write-wars with Berkay's DPS/Excel workflow, no silent base-expiry corruption.

knobs.name: T_grace + verify_schedule
knobs.value: 15 min; P0 draws +4/+8/+14; extend +19/+24; STUCK only on actually-OLD-classified draws (missing draws extend timers, not STUCK); then 10-min probes to +60; error clock from grace end
knobs.why: Measured propagation 2-10 min. 'No data' and 'old rule' are now distinct: outages extend, only observed old generations alarm — kills the false-STUCK path during relay drops.

knobs.name: TURB_WIN
knobs.value: 30 min after ANY write (loop or external); inside it, confirmation is demanded only for SURPRISING draws — expected post-write positions pass on one draw
knobs.why: The draw lottery is write-correlated (30/30 identical quiet, 1.3-2.8% splits near writes). Scoping confirmation to surprises keeps burst-day verify cost from doubling.

knobs.name: M freshness
knobs.value: M <= 10 min at DECIDE (history cannot predict M); ladder cache <= 30 min (competitors draw-stable); BURST exception: M reuse <= 60 min with buffer widened 0.45%/h x age
knobs.why: Fresh M where precision matters; in a correlated market move, direction matters more than precision, so spending ~1% extra discount instead of a probe halves burst probe cost.

knobs.name: decide_bundle + split rule
knobs.value: 2 draws 60-120 s apart, per-draw k; TOL_GEN 0.35% agreement -> mean; 3rd draw on split; 3-way split -> max(M) for ONE_SIDED, median+provisional for STRICT_FLOOR
knobs.why: Two agreeing draws defeat the episodic lottery at minimum cost; conservatism is now contract-directional — max(M) was anti-conservative toward the floor side of two-sided intents.

knobs.name: implied_M_plausibility + fallback
knobs.value: [0.985, 1.11]; if ALL candidates implausible -> immediate free FMX re-read first; FMX unchanged + 2nd implausible draw -> DATA_ANOMALY alert
knobs.why: Observed M range [1.0065, 1.0853] plus headroom; the fallback gives step V2 a defined branch where v1 had none, and routes ghost-writes to the right alarm.

knobs.name: b_drift (placement buffer)
knobs.value: CRITICAL 0.75% @ 60 min; ACTIVE one-sided 2.0% @ 240 min; ACTIVE strict-floor 1.5% @ 180 min; TAIL 1440 min; +0.5% per confirmed fail (cap 2.5%); DEGRADED adds 0.45%/h x blind time
knobs.why: Buffer must cover drift over (interval + ~15 min latency): 0.45%/h x 4.25 h = 1.91% < 2.0% and x 3.25 h = 1.46% < 1.5% — the v1 ACTIVE tier was arithmetically short by its own formula. One-sided cells buy safety with depth; strict-floor cells buy it with cadence.

knobs.name: probe_budget
knobs.value: Global token bucket refill 2/min, burst 6; P0 verify > P1 correct/decide > P2 critical > P3 active > P4 tail; deferral visible, never silent. Steady state ~0.9/min at 20/100/200 cells
knobs.why: Hard 429 discipline through one relay + one Cloud Run instance; priorities guarantee verification never starves behind routine monitoring.

knobs.name: single_draw_trust + 3-sigma waiver
knobs.value: Trust 1 draw iff not TURBULENT, M in [0.985,1.11], no flips, |dM| <= 2%; otherwise confirm in 60-120 s — EXCEPT violations > 3 x sigma_cell act on one draw
knobs.why: Quiet windows are deterministic, so routine probes cost 1 draw; but a 5-8% competitor move is not a lottery artifact (competitors never vary) — demanding confirmation there wastes the scarce resource on correlated days.

knobs.name: M_ewma
knobs.value: alpha 0.3 steady; landing draws set only a provisional M; first post-TURB_WIN draw REPLACES it (alpha = 1)
knobs.why: Landing draws are taken inside the lottery window; re-baselining from the first quiet draw stops a turbulent M from steering the next 3-4 corrections.

knobs.name: DRIFT_WATCH preempt
knobs.value: Margin < 0.75% of T AND 3 consecutive post-gap adverse probes -> in-band correction in EITHER direction; crossing the band top requires confirmed FAIL
knobs.why: Ramps caught pre-violation cost ~0 error minutes; bidirectional in-band matches production's sanctioned upward floor correction (SCAN's one exception) — discount-only bought floor-side violation minutes for nothing.

knobs.name: REWRITE_MIN
knobs.value: 45 min between writes to one cell; VOID on confirmed FAIL and BURST triage; hygiene never waived
knobs.why: Every write opens a fresh propagation lottery — chasing drift manufactures error minutes; but anti-churn must never outrank fixing a confirmed violation (the v1 deadlock).

knobs.name: BURST mode
knobs.value: Enter: >=8 flips/30 min or same competitor on >=5 cells; SUSPECT propagation via shared adjacent-duration ladders; revenue-at-risk ranking; sampled verify (top decile full schedule, rest 1 draw, failures escalate batch); ~264 draws / 2.2 h for 120 cells
knobs.why: The binding constraint is the correlated day. Exploiting exact-ladders-per-draw, ladder sharing, and sampled verification cuts a 5-h saturation to 2.2 h with top revenue fixed in 30 min: ~5-8% burst-day error vs 15-25% unmitigated, ledgered honestly as an episode.

knobs.name: DEGRADED (blind-time rule)
knobs.value: t_blind from relay heartbeat; buffer +0.45%/h of blindness; >20 min freeze non-P0 writes + extend timers; >30 min alert + relay kick runbook; blind minutes ledgered UNMONITORED, never counted clean; recovery = P1 re-baseline, CRITICAL first
knobs.why: The measured system loses its relay for 20-40 min exactly on mass-write days. Claims that assume 100% measurement uptime are false claims; blind time must widen buffers and appear in the ledger, not masquerade as monitored-clean.

knobs.name: escalation
knobs.value: 2 confirmed fails/24 h -> CRITICAL + b_drift +0.5% (cap 2.5%); 3 -> operator alert with achievable-contract quote, hold at conservative edge; 48 h clean -> decay; BURST episodes count once per STATION
knobs.why: Cells whose M volatility exceeds the band need buffer or renegotiation, not more writes; per-station burst counting stops one market move from mass-escalating 120 cells into CRITICAL and blowing the probe budget.

v2.claimed_error: All rates are on the DISPLAY plane (whole francs + list order, the shopper's view), hour-integrated over the RC_TIMES pickup-rung distribution, excluding the 15-min grace, with blind time reported separately as UNMONITORED (never counted clean). By contract class: (1) ONE_SIDED default ("displayed strictly under C1 at every pickup hour"): CRITICAL tier ~1.5-3% of shopper moments; ACTIVE ~3-6%. Derivation: hour spread is paid in margin, not error (worst-band aiming costs a mean extra discount of roughly delta_hour/2, up to ~3.4% at the measured 6.85% spread — a visible, chosen cost); ramps (<=~0.5%/h measured) are caught by DRIFT_WATCH at ~0 error minutes; residual error = step events beyond the buffer (<=1-2/day measured, adverse half only), each costing at most tier interval + ~3 min confirm/write - 15 min grace (<=~48 min/event at CRITICAL), roughly halved by buffer absorption. (2) STRICT_FLOOR two-sided: offered only where delta_hour <= band width; ~2-4% at CRITICAL with the 180-min ACTIVE cadence. (3) HOUR_CONDITIONAL (explicit opt-in): ~1-2.5% of canonical-band moments ONLY — deliberately NOT a claim about all shoppers, and labeled as such in UI and ledger. (4) Burst days (correlated competitor repricing): ~5-8% violation-minutes on affected cells for that day (vs ~15-25% unmitigated), ledgered as a named episode and excluded from steady-state figures. (5) Campaign transitions: ~0 systematic error — per-draw k eliminates the overshoot class; residual flips are ordinary step events. Irreducible floor: the 1-franc display quantum + 0.35% generation wobble + (pre-calibration) unknown tie ordering mean no policy places finer than ~one displayed franc; intents narrower than the quantized gate are refused or run as NEAREST_ACHIEVABLE with dual accounting, and equal-franc ties count against us until the tie rule is measured. Assumptions: M dynamics as measured 2026-08-29/30 (quiet-window determinism; drift <=~0.5%/h; steps <=~3.6%, <=2/day; M in [0.99,1.09]; hour spread <=7% prior); campaign always flagged via 'before'; competitors draw-stable within a draw; propagation <=15 min for >=90% of writes (excess surfaces as STUCK from OLD-classified draws and its post-grace time is counted); the 2/min probe bucket honored; the 5-min FMX poll operational (external-edit exposure bounded by poll cadence); relay outages handled by DEGRADED semantics rather than assumed away. The C3 ledger publishes realized vs claimed per tier and per contract continuously — every number above is falsifiable in production within days, by design.

sim.method: Event-driven Monte Carlo (Python, zero_error_sim.py, ran to completion in ~22 s). World model built strictly from the measured facts: per cell, 6 hour-planes ("(date,hour) cache keys") each carrying its own multiplier M; piecewise-constant jumps at Poisson rate 3/day/plane with magnitudes {45% zero, 30% ±1.3–2.8%, 17% ±3.5%, 8% ±6.9%}, mild pull toward 1.045, clamped to [0.99,1.10]; shopper weight afternoon-heavy (per the 19-rung UI); competitors constant; whole-franc display rounding for shoppers, 2-decimal API values for the console; episodic 50/50 two-generation lottery only inside propagation windows (U(2,10) min, 10% up to 20) after each FMX write; GM-only flagged campaign ×0.88 redrawn daily at 07:00 with P=0.15. 40 cells (C1∈[80,250], rule depths (1+r)∈{0.2152,0.5,0.8,1.2}) × 60 days, common random worlds across policies. ERROR = shopper-weighted fraction of non-grace time with displayed GM ≥ displayed C1 (T_grace=15 min post-write). Also tracked: floor-breach % (S<F=max(0.95C1,C1−10), campaign-off time only), margin give-up vs point-pricing at T=0.97C1, corrections and probes per cell-day, and fleet size that fits the 4-probe/min 429 budget. Policies: P0 = today's console (daily 09:00 point re-aim, no loop); P1 = Architect v2 reconstructed faithfully from its spec fragments (band [F,T], aim mid-band, canonical-hour EWMA M_hat, 2-draw confirm +5 min, DEADBAND 0.6 rule-points, verify +4/+8/+14, TURBULENT 30, k_policy=0.88 iff ≥2 of last 4 draws in 24h flagged, 17c 30-min flag stability, plausibility [0.985,1.11]); P2 = one static write at 0.99·T/1.10; P3 = P1 + aim buffer 0.5/1/1.5/2/3%; P4 = repaired loop (rotating-plane monitor, per-plane M estimates, shelf sets the WORST plane at the aim, per-draw campaign flag on the pre-discount basis — never counteracts a flagged campaign, shelf-relative deadband 0.3% with rank-override, free FMX r_live reads before DECIDE). The six Adversary scenarios ran as targeted stress sims (scen 1, 2, 3, 5 simulated; 4 and 6 semi-analytic with mini-sim numbers). A sensitivity world (60% common fleet drift, avg plane spread 6.4% vs 9.1%) checks model dependence.

Its load-bearing knobs, each verified against a specific failure: (1) rotate the monitored hour-plane and keep per-plane M estimates, set the FMX rule so the WORST plane lands at the aim — kills the 19-45% plane-blindness error that no probe-rate increase fixes; (2) campaign k from the CURRENT draw's flag, decisions on the pre-discount basis, never counteract a flagged campaign — deletes scenario 2 entirely; (3) deadband in shelf-% (0.3%), not rule-points, with rank-override — deletes the deep-discount deadlock; (4) free FMX r_live read before every DECIDE and on any implausible draw — deletes ghost-write blindness; (5) competitor readings are noise-free (measured), so competitor-driven corrections need 1 draw, not 2 — cuts market-move Monday from 13.8% to 3.6%. Margin knob is a policy choice on one axis: aim worst plane at T=0.97C1 -> 0.05%/6.7% margin cost; aim 0.99*C1 -> ~0.2%/4.9% (3.7% in the mild-spread world). Recommend aim=T for CRITICAL cells, 0.99*C1 for volume cells, probe 30 min, T_grace 15.

P4 under the same attacks: 28 min, 12 min, 0 min, 3.6%, bounded by K*interval. Irreducible floor: P4's residual 0.02-0.1% is detection latency on ±3.5-6.9% jumps between rotating probes plus campaign/market transition lag — it scales ~linearly with probe interval and cannot reach 0 under the 4-6/min relay ceiling; and the FULL intent (floor 0.95C1 AND rank <C1 on every hour-plane with ONE FMX rule) is infeasible ~95% of the time because the measured hour-plane spread (6.85% observed; 6-9% modeled) exceeds the 5.26% intent window — rank error can go to ~0, rank+floor simultaneously cannot, for any policy.
sim.caveats: (1) P1 is a reconstruction from the Architect-v2 fragments quoted in the adversary scenarios (deadband 0.6 pts, mid-band aim, canonical hour, k window rule, 17c, plausibility bounds, verify +4/+8/+14); if the real spec differs, P1's numbers move — but its three structural failures (plane blindness, k-window/17c double ownership, rule-point deadband) are logic properties, not parameter choices. (2) The pivotal unmeasured quantity is the cross-hour-plane spread: only ONE 6.85% pair was measured live. My main world (independent planes, avg spread 9.1%) is the worst-case reading; the 60%-common-drift world (6.4%) cuts P1's error to 14% and P4's margin cost to 3.7-5.4% but changes no ranking. A one-day hour survey (~2 draws/hour-band, ~50 draws total, within budget) would pin this down and is the single highest-value measurement to run next. (3) Floor-breach % is large for every rank-safe policy — that is the quantified irreducible trade-off above, not a bug; campaign-on time is excluded from floor accounting (flagged, exogenous). (4) rentalcars' rounding rule (half-up vs truncate) and tie-breaking are unmeasured; at C1<80 the 1-franc quantum is ~2% of the band, so P4 aims C1d−1.51 there — ties counted as violations throughout. (5) P0 was modeled charitably (daily re-aim; a write-and-forget P0 is strictly worse). (6) Scenarios 4 and 6 are mini-sim/analytic, not full 60-day MC; scenario 5 assumes the documented 20-40 min 429 outage hits once at 09:00. (7) MC noise: P4's 0.02-0.14% figures are small counts over 40 cells x 60 days — read them as "low single-digit basis points", not exact; all policies faced identical worlds (common random numbers). (8) Margin% counts only give-up below T; P4@0.99C1 prices ABOVE the stated 97-target while staying under C1 — rank-faithful but a deviation from the literal 97/100 intent the operator should sign off on.

resolved: Q1/S1 DEADBAND dimensional deadlock — RESOLVED by S1: v1 = 959 min mean / 2628 min p95 per event (95% of events exceed the claimed bound); shelf-relative deadband = 28 min mean / 34 p95, inside v2's own <=48 min/event CRITICAL envelope. v2's J-space quantum claim independently verified: 0.01 FMX rule-point = 0.0465% shelf at (1+r)=0.2152, so an exact solve is always expressible; DEADBAND+REWRITE_MIN void on confirmed FAIL deletes the 'already in band' deadlock path.

Q2 binding plane / rounding — RESOLVED: the pre-calibration target P_api <= min(floor(C1)-0.01, round(C1)-0.51) is analytically safe under both trunc and half-up (worst-case intersection, no sim needed), and S3's data precondition is already satisfied — rc-price-comparison-protocol memory holds >=8 recorded API-decimal/displayed-franc pairs (114.95->115, 120.95->121, 122.45->122, 126.97->127; struck 130.62->131, 137.44->137, 139.15->139, 144.28->144), all consistent with half-up, so rho can be seeded on Day 0 from existing records rather than assumed.

Q3/S6 domain hole + inverted band — RESOLVED by S6: v1 refused every C1 < ~76 CHF (C1=52.49: band 1.05 < gate 1.36) and misdiagnosed C1=400 (F=390 > T=388); v2's quantized gate passes C1=52.49 (francs {50,51}, W~1.6 >= 0.6 required — arithmetic checked) and the P4 analog holds ~0.02% error at +2.9% margin on exactly those cells; floor-wins point-contract semantics verified against production memory pricing-band-2026-08-28 ('factor = min(targets) clamped up to max(floors)').

Q4/S3 hour-plane blindness — RESOLVED as mechanism by S3 + main sweep: canonical-hour v1 loses 45% of shopper moments while self-reporting ~0; worst-plane aiming + hour rotation = 0.02-0.14% at 15-60 min; v2's ACTIVE claim of 3-6% at 240 min is consistent with the sim's ~linear interval scaling (extrapolates to ~0.4-0.5%), i.e. conservative. The MARGIN side of this answer is NOT resolved (open risk 4).

final.spec:
SPEC v3 — FINAL, IMPLEMENTATION DOCUMENT. Supersedes v2. Folds in the simulation-chosen knob values (P4 best config) and closes adversary risks R1–R7: R2/R6 closed by mechanism, R1/R4/R5/R7 closed by process gates written into this spec, R3 open-by-measurement with a scheduled survey, plus six named irreducible floors (PART 9).

PART 0 — GOVERNANCE, ROLLOUT MODES, CLAIM DISCIPLINE (closes R1, R4, R5, R7)

0.1 Modes. MODE_SHADOW (default at ship): all sensors, DECIDE, MONITOR, VERIFY-of-operator-writes and the C3 ledger run; the loop writes NOTHING; every would-be write is logged as a counterfactual proposal {aim, J, predicted violation-minutes saved}.
